content: A low-grade fever is typically defined as a body temperature of approximately 38.5 degrees Celsius (about 101 degrees Fahrenheit). It is considered a non-specific clinical finding, meaning it is not unique to a single condition but can be observed in a wide range of diseases. These conditions include infectious causes, such as viral illnesses or infective endocarditis, as well as autoimmune disorders and malignant diseases. The presence of a persistent low-grade fever may indicate an underlying illness and warrants further investigation to determine its cause.
